In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aldo‐ keto reductase superfamily evolved in the early stages of life and is involved in the detoxiﬁcation of reactive aldehydes.

the AKR superfamily of detoxification enzymes has a very old evolutionary history, and that the nonhyperbolic kinetics of some of these enzymes may be an adaptation mechanism to high levels of reactive oxygen species.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a novel AKR in cyanobacteria that is highly similar to human AKRs and is capable of reducing lipid peroxidation and advanced glycation products.
the cyanobacterial AKR AKR3G is the founding member of a novel subfamily with a high potential for xenobiotic detoxification and is a good candidate for further studies on detoxification in bacteria.
the AKR3 subfamily is the most ancient one and has been conserved during evolution.

the aldo‐ketoreductase superfamily is not only involved in the detoxication of xenobiotics, but also in the reduction of lipid peroxidative products and advanced glycosylation products in the body, and that the non‐hyperbolic enzyme kinetic behavior observed with some substraties might be an evolutionary adaptation mechanism to higher levels of oxidative stress in the body.
